frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the number of international tourists, measured in millions, who traveled to five different regions worldwide in 1990, 1995, 2000 and 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, global tourist numbers rose significantly over the 15-year period, with all regions experiencing growth except America, which saw a slight decline towards the end. Additionally, Europe consistently attracted the highest number of visitors, while Asia and the Pacific recorded the most significant increase.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the most popular destinations, Europe dominated with 280.2 million arrivals in 1990, approximately 3.5 times higher than America at 80.5 million, while Asia and the Pacific stood at 60.2 million. By 2005, Europe's figure had risen steadily to 400.2 million, maintaining its leading position. Meanwhile, America's numbers increased to a peak of 118.2 million in 2000 before falling slightly to 113.2 million at the end of the period. In contrast, Asia and the Pacific witnessed remarkable growth, more than doubling to reach 135.8 million in 2005, thereby surpassing America.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining regions, Africa recorded 18.2 million tourists in 1990, nearly double that of the Middle East at 9.8 million. Both regions followed a consistent upward trend throughout the period, with Africa's figure rising to 28.7 million and the Middle East reaching 15.8 million by 2005, representing increases of approximately 10.5 and 6 million, respectively.
